questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The curriculum. I wanted courses that matched what I wanted to write about in my master's thesis.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great. Great teachers, great dorm, great help, great everything.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Super easy. Chuo's website was easy to navigate and had all the information I needed. When I was still in doubt, then the international center was quick to answer my emails. 10/10.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was a master's student so I didn't get a study helper (a Japanese student to help you acclimate to JP etc.), but it seems bachelor students do, which sounds like a great system. I had loads of help to find in the dorm manager where I lived and the international center on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: If I ever had a question it was super easy to get answered and people were super sweet and helpful.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did it through the university. Just follow their procedures and do the off-campus dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Dependant on your campus, you might have 1 hour+ long commutes, and it costs a wee bit to use the train that much, but if you get a commuter pass, then it's not that bad. You can also you the commuter pass for personal travel and acutally end up saving quite a lot of money.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My dorm was outfitted with small private apartments, great privacy. There was a lobby where students could then meet up if they wanted to.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just follow the links you get sent on e-mail.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to pre-register for some courses due to congestion risk, but it was no problem and everyone who signed up got the courses they wanted. Otherwise, you just follow the online procedures, and it is very intutitive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International Center. An on-campus office that helped with any question you had. They were honestly great, super sweet and easy to talk to. Great English as well, so no worries communicating.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all I wanted, as did everyone else.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't miss the deadlines. I was placed in a Japanese language class that conflicted with my scheduled other courses, and I was allowed to change my Japanese class to one of higher level to accomodate my schedule; the university is more flexible than you think.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great teachers, all relevant topics.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were spot on. Not too hard not too easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is a seminar style way of teaching so lots of discussions, which is about the same as TORS faculty style at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Constituional Law, Introduction to Japanese Law, Law and Business in Japan, Law and Society 2, Japanese Advanced 2.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to JP law and Law and Business in JP. Super relevant hands-on knowledge about navigating the legal side of business in Japan.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay an additional National Health Insurance Policy, which is about 1000 yen pr. month; 50 kr. ca.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was super cheap. Everything was super cheap, but that's cause the yen was weak when I went. In general eat out at restaurants and drinking is very cheap though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dorm assistants (Japanese students), held a lot of events, which was great to get to know them and the other exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were club circles, but I never joined those, but I believe you could. Otherwise, it was mostly events held by the residents assistants at my dorm, and the university wrote out about events that were happening in Tokyo that you could join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Make friends with the Japanese students in your dorm. They will create fun events and take you to interesting places in Tokyo.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Look for event posters around the stations. It's a good way to see what is going on in Tokyo at the moment.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. I've been to Japan 3 times before though. They speak quite good English in Tokyo though, so shouldn't be an issue.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get Line and Instagram. They are the main communication tools.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food, if you eat out a lot, can be quite heavy. Lots of deep friend stuff.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How polite everyone was.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make friends with the Japanese students, say yes to everything (a bad experience in the moment, becomes a fun story in the future,) bring clothes for summer and winter.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go in with an open mind.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people. I made some great friends and had some great experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The food. If you eat out a lot, then be prepared to not eat a lot of vegetables. The food was delicious, and amazing, but after 2 months of eating out everyday (it was super cheap), then you'll begin to miss vegetables.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was great. I cannot recommend Chuo University enough!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
